newsitem.title: UK: UK insurers lag in professionalism, training.
newsitem.headline: UK insurers lag in professionalism, training.

text.p: UK insurers are lagging behind their overseas counterparts in their professionalism in several key areas, a leading insurance executive said.

"The insurance industry in the UK must set its sights high, as it must be recognised that the UK as a whole has lagged behind, compared with other countries, on education and training," said John Carter, chief executive of UK insurer Commercial Union and chairman of the Association of British Insurers.

Speaking at the annual conference of the Chartered Insurance Institute in Newcastle, Carter said, "The UK insurance industry must increasingly compare itself with the best managed industries in the world, not just with insurance industries in other countries."

"Some parts of the industry are poor at giving responsibility and challenges early enough to good quality staff. Promotion needs to occur at a more rapid pace if the best available talent is to be attracted," he said.
Carter called for managers in the industry and in the civil service departments which regulate insurance to make more use of secondments in each others' businesses and in sectors outside insurance.
Carter also criticised the weak links between the insurance industry and academic teaching and research.

"The insurance industry suffers from a lack of academic research. It's not surprising therefore that we find it difficult to commision research, because few academics have been encouraged to take an interest.
"We are the losers in this," Carter said.
